text: Clandestine shrines of the southern Yellow Turbans, unique to Wu Huan.
Hidden congregations that nurture the southern spark, generating Embers and teaching the faithful to strike from cover.
Deep in the hills of Jiangdong, where the Yellow Sky was never raised, a handful of believers meet by night. The word is passed quietly, from farmer to fisherman, and the first embers begin to glow.
A hidden meeting place for the faithful of the south.
The congregation grows. Grain and news move along paths the Han magistrates do not know, and those who shelter here learn the hills as well as any hunter.
Nurture the southern spark and spread the Way.
No longer a secret whispered between neighbours, the shrine draws pilgrims from across the southern commanderies. What was a spark on the wind is now a steady flame.
A sanctuary where the faithful gather in secret.
The sanctuary is the beating heart of the southern rising. Its faithful are many, its paths are hidden, and the Han lapdogs who come looking seldom return.
The heart of the southern rebellion.
The Yellow Sky burns over Jiangdong at last. What Wu Huan nursed for years alone has spread beyond any hope of quenching - an inferno that will consume the south.
The spark has become an inferno.
